subject: Late token loss during dedicated pool failover — remediation & customer bridge
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmarket.ai>, BrightMarket Ops <ops@brightmarket.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Late token loss during dedicated pool failover — immediate update

Hi Elena / BrightMarket ops team,

I wanted to reach out with an immediate update and apologize for the disruption you saw earlier today (09:02–09:28 PST) where a subset of requests experienced late token loss during a scheduled warm-standby failover in your dedicated GPU pool. We know some of your inference calls returned truncated outputs or "incomplete token" artifacts, and that is unacceptable.

What we know so far:
- Trigger: warm-standby failover process while autoscaler reconciled reserved nodes.
- Symptom: ~17 minutes total window with intermittent truncated responses and increased 5xx rates for roughly 4% of requests.
- Scope: BrightMarket tenant on us-west-2 reserved pool only; no other customers were impacted.

Immediate mitigations already applied:
1) Rolled back the standby reconciliation to previous stable state at 09:29 PST.
2) Disabled the new micro-eviction heuristic for your pool to prevent further KV-cache invalidations.
3) Enabled temporary prefix-anchoring for long-running chat sessions for BrightMarket to avoid partial KV replay.

Next steps we are executing (ETA attached in postmortem draft):
- Ben and Soojin are extracting token stream logs and metrics snapshots for all affected sessions (deliver by EOD 09 Jan).
- We'll share a short postmortem draft and a remediation plan with rollback-safe mitigations by 11 Jan.
- Offering 10% usage credit for impacted window; we'll confirm credit calculation details in the follow-up.

I know you need clarity on impact and assurances that this won't recur. We will provide: explicit RCA, long-term corrective actions around the failover path, and a timeline for formal code-level fixes.

If you have a preferred time for a quick sync (15–20m) tomorrow, Ben and I can join.

Apologies again — we take this seriously and will keep you updated every step of the way.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmarket.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMarket Ops <ops@brightmarket.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Late token loss during dedicated pool failover — immediate update

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the quick note.

Concrete questions from our side:
- Rough count: how many sessions were truncated? We saw sporadic user-facing errors in our prod telemetry and want to align counts before the credit calc.
- Is there any risk of data leakage between sessions during the failure? (we observed no obvious cross-session tokens but need confirmation)
- Prefer a 30m sync tomorrow to walk through logs — 10:30am PST works for us.

We expect the postmortem and credit calc by 11 Jan. If the scope is larger than the pool, escalate.

— Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform, BrightMarket

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmarket.ai>, BrightMarket Ops <ops@brightmarket.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Late token loss during dedicated pool failover — immediate update

Elena / team — following up with the first batch of findings.

Summary (short):
- Affected sessions: ~1,220 distinct sessions across the BrightMarket tenant during the window. We classify ~950 as short-form requests (under 128 tokens) and ~270 as long-form streaming sessions where partial KV replay caused truncated outputs.
- No evidence of token leakage across session IDs; internal correlation checks show session IDs remained isolated. We will include signed hashes in the postmortem artifact for your verification.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): an ordering race during the warm-standby failover path where the KV cache flush and live-stream handoff overlapped for streaming sessions. The micro-eviction heuristic caused early KV invalidation prior to handoff completion.

Action items we completed today:
- Attached: metrics_snapshot_20270109.png with token error rate, 5xxs, and tail-latency graphs.
- Created postmortem draft (redwood_postmortem_draft_v1.pdf) and uploaded to the shared drive link.
- Immediate code mitigation: queued a patch to serialize KV flush then handoff; safe rollback tested on canary cluster (target merge 2027-01-12).

Requesting: Elena, please confirm if you want us to proceed with a forced rolling restart of your reserved nodes during a low-traffic window (we can orchestrate and own the maintenance) or prefer a patch-first approach.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: metrics_snapshot_20270109.png

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmarket.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMarket Ops <ops@brightmarket.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Late token loss during dedicated pool failover — immediate update

Thanks Ben — that helps. Confirming:
- We saw ~1.1k affected sessions in our telemetry (numbers align closely).
- No user data cross-pollination observed. Good to hear about signed hashes — we'll verify once posted.
- Prefer patch-first; we want to avoid restarts during current campaign. Schedule the merge and let us know the planned canary timeline.

We also want a written commit that you will:
1) Deliver the RCA and a final postmortem by 2027-01-14.
2) Apply the serialization fix to canary on 2027-01-11 and to production by 2027-01-12 (if canary passes).
3) Confirm final credit amount before 2027-01-14.

Our legal team also requested a short note about whether logs for the affected window will be retained for 90 days for their audit.

— Elena

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmarket.ai>, BrightMarket Ops <ops@brightmarket.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Late token loss during dedicated pool failover — immediate update

Elena — quick status update following canary verification and postmortem draft delivery.

1) Canary verification completed (2027-01-11, successful): the serialization patch eliminated the KV-flush/handoff race on canary clusters; no truncated stream artifacts observed across 24h synthetic replay.
2) Production rollout: patch merged and staged 2027-01-12 04:30 PST; progressive rollout completed by 10:15 PST with health checks green.
3) Postmortem: uploaded redwood_postmortem_draft_v1.pdf to the shared drive (link above). This draft contains timeline, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and the longer-term plan to add stronger invariants in the failover orchestration.
4) Credits: we've prepared a draft credit calculation (10% usage credit for the impacted window) and will finalize once you confirm the session counts.
5) Logs: we will retain the full request/response logs for the affected window for 90 days and provide access to your security contact.

We committed to the dates you requested and will send the finalized postmortem and the formal credits summary by 2027-01-14.

If you'd like a wrap-up call Friday, Ben and I can join.

Thanks for working with us through this.

— Soojin (on behalf of the SRE and TAM teams)
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_postmortem_draft_v1.pdf
